title: Copilot Dynamic Workflows
summary: A recently introduced, code-defined orchestration option to evaluate for the pilot.

sections.label: Verified capability
sections.text: The 1 October 2026 announcement covers Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, and SDK. Workflows can mix deterministic steps, agents, tools, structured results, and review checkpoints. Status: public preview.

sections.label: Scope
sections.text: Do not assume the same feature is available directly in IntelliJ’s interface. Check the actual client and enterprise policy before selecting it.

sections.label: Limits and permissions
sections.text: Documented credit limits are approximate because usage is reported after it occurs. Extension code can run outside subagent permission prompts; runner credentials and sandbox controls still matter.

sections.label: Decision
sections.text: Try a small, versioned workflow with fixed inputs and recorded outputs. Compare its maintainability and recovery behavior with existing Jenkins/Atlassian automation.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended use: Assess the documented candidate in the actual client and compare it with existing automation.
Record the installed client, feature access and organization policy separately from the article.
Run a bounded workflow and retain actual state, permission and recovery observations.
Workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Existing examples, tenant availability, older product claims and comparative benefits were not revalidated by this mapping review.

confidence: High for capability; unknown for tenant fit

catalog.applicability: Use when evaluating Copilot's code-defined workflow option for a pilot. Check the actual client, enterprise policy, credit limits and runner permissions first, then compare a small versioned workflow with existing automation.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
